title: The Spiritual Armament
english: He loosens the hands of warriors, and a negligent monk destroys the zeal of brothers. A swarm of bees produces wax, and a community of brothers produces the kingdom of heaven. A trumpet awakens the zeal of warriors, and the diligence of disciples is the teaching of practical virtue.

Arm, O leader, your brothers with the words of rings, and protect them with promises of coming good things; surround them with the shield of faith through contests, and hem them in with the hope that is toward God. Move the feet in evangelical lessons and vivify the loins with words of temperance; give a sword into the hand against the passions, a sharper spirit, and nce in the battle; and show them to be fearsome.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG De magistris et discipulis u01-rem-early

title: The Teacher as Physician
english: The lesser [punishment] by the threat of eternal punishment. The victor is proclaimed with bright praises, for I know that even praise makes [men] more diligent; and the one influenced, treat [him] sympathetically, for the prudent man does not incur a lesser threat through forgiveness. Let [the teacher] not be moved in mind against a disciple having sinned, for one does not call himself holy before the treatment of another; but rather, without malice, correct toward the good; for indeed a physician treats the passion, but does not feel indignation toward one who has become ill through carelessness. A physician, while cutting, does this without anger; and a teacher, while reproving, let him not let his mind be mixed with the reproof. title: The Path to Virtue
english: It is a small thing to train toward self-control and toward those beginning in virtue. Pitch a tent for Aileim, and the gates themselves are interpreted, carrying a sign for the entrance into virtue, and show the seventy phoenixes. Pitch a tent according to the twelve springs—for the phoenixes must also shout your victory, and the waters providing a flame that comforts the passions richly—until all the foreign nations, quenching everything, reach the land of promise (Hebrews 11:10), in which they will live the blessed life of apatheia, receiving as a reward for their labors the true joy.
